symptom: PC1 cannot ping PC2 even though both PCs should be in the same VLAN
show_output: show vlan brief: VLAN 10 active; Fa0/1 is in VLAN 10; Fa0/2 is in VLAN 20
expected_fault: PC2 is assigned to the wrong VLAN
expected_fix: Assign Fa0/2 to VLAN 10

symptom: A PC connected to the switch cannot communicate with any device in VLAN 20
topology: PC1 -> SW1; PC1 should be connected to VLAN 20
show_output: show vlan brief: VLAN 10 active; VLAN 20 is not present; Fa0/5 is assigned to VLAN 10
expected_fault: VLAN 20 is missing from the switch
expected_fix: Create VLAN 20 and assign the correct switch port

symptom: Devices in VLAN 10 on different switches cannot communicate
show_output: show interfaces trunk: SW1 Fa0/24 trunking; allowed VLANs: 1,20,30
expected_fault: VLAN 10 is not allowed on the trunk
expected_fix: Allow VLAN 10 on the trunk between the switches

symptom: Devices across a trunk have intermittent or failed communication after VLAN configuration changes
show_output: show interfaces trunk: SW1 native VLAN 99; SW2 native VLAN 1
expected_fault: Native VLAN mismatch exists between the two trunk interfaces
expected_fix: Configure the same native VLAN on both trunk interfaces

symptom: PC receives an IP address but cannot ping devices outside its local subnet
topology: PC1 -> SW1 -> R1 -> Server; PC1 is in VLAN 10
expected_fault: PC1 has a default gateway from the wrong subnet
expected_fix: Set the PC default gateway to 192.168.10.1

symptom: PC can communicate with devices in its local network but cannot reach the router or remote networks
expected_fault: The PC has no default gateway configured
expected_fix: Configure the PC with the correct default gateway

symptom: Multiple PCs in VLAN 10 cannot reach remote networks
show_output: show ip interface brief: G0/0 192.168.20.1/24 up/up; PC subnet: 192.168.10.0/24
expected_fault: The router interface is configured for a different subnet than the connected PCs
expected_fix: Configure the router interface with the correct IP address and subnet

symptom: PC does not receive an IP address from the DHCP server
topology: PC1 -> SW1 -> R1; DHCP server is on another network
show_output: show ip dhcp pool: Network 192.168.20.0/24; PC VLAN network: 192.168.10.0/24
expected_fault: DHCP pool is configured for the wrong network
expected_fix: Configure the DHCP pool for the correct client network

symptom: New PCs in VLAN 20 receive no IP address
show_output: show running-config: no ip dhcp pool VLAN20; VLAN 20 gateway is 192.168.20.1
expected_fault: No DHCP pool exists for VLAN 20
expected_fix: Create a DHCP pool for VLAN 20 with the correct network and gateway

symptom: PCs in a remote VLAN receive APIPA addresses instead of DHCP addresses
topology: PC1 -> SW1 -> R1 -> DHCP Server; DHCP server is on 192.168.30.0/24
show_output: show running-config interface vlan 10: no ip helper-address configured; DHCP server: 192.168.30.10
expected_fault: DHCP relay configuration is missing on the client VLAN interface
expected_fix: Configure ip helper-address 192.168.30.10 on the VLAN interface

symptom: Some PCs receive DHCP addresses but new PCs cannot obtain an address
show_output: show ip dhcp pool: Total addresses 50; Leased addresses 50
expected_fault: The DHCP address pool has no available addresses
expected_fix: Increase the available DHCP address range or add another appropriate DHCP pool

symptom: PC can ping the web server by IP address but cannot access it using its hostname
topology: PC1 -> SW1 -> R1 -> DNS Server and Web Server
show_output: PC1 IP: 192.168.10.25; DNS Server: 192.168.20.20; ping 192.168.20.30 succeeds; ping webserver.local fails
expected_fault: PC is configured with an incorrect DNS server address
expected_fix: Configure the PC to use the correct DNS server

symptom: Multiple PCs can reach the DNS server by IP address but hostname resolution fails
show_output: ping 192.168.20.20 succeeds; nslookup webserver.local: DNS request timed out
expected_fault: The DNS service is unavailable or not responding
expected_fix: Verify that the DNS service is enabled and running on the DNS server

symptom: PC can resolve some hostnames but cannot resolve the internal web server hostname
topology: PC1 -> SW1 -> R1 -> DNS Server -> Web Server
show_output: nslookup mail.local succeeds; nslookup webserver.local: Non-existent domain
expected_fault: DNS record for webserver.local is missing
expected_next_command: show running-config or inspect DNS records
expected_fix: Create the missing DNS record for webserver.local

symptom: PC1 can reach its local router but cannot reach the server network behind R2
topology: PC1 -> R1 -> R2 -> Server; R1 and R2 are connected by a routed link
show_output: show ip route: R1 has connected routes for 192.168.10.0/24 and 10.0.0.0/30 but no route to 192.168.30.0/24
expected_fault: R1 is missing a static route to the server network
expected_fix: Add a static route to 192.168.30.0/24 using R2 as the next hop

symptom: Traffic from R1 to the remote network is sent to the wrong router
show_output: show ip route: S 192.168.30.0/24 [1/0] via 10.0.0.6; R2 address on R1 link: 10.0.0.2
expected_fault: Static route uses an incorrect next-hop address
expected_fix: Change the static route to use the correct next-hop address

symptom: PC1 cannot reach the remote server even though a static route exists
show_output: show ip route: S 192.168.30.0/24 via 10.0.0.2; actual server network: 192.168.40.0/24
expected_fault: Static route points to the wrong destination network
expected_fix: Configure a static route for the correct destination network

symptom: A static route appears in the configuration but traffic is not forwarded through it
show_output: show ip route: S 192.168.30.0/24 is directly connected via GigabitEthernet0/1; GigabitEthernet0/1 is down
expected_fault: Static route depends on an interface that is down
expected_fix: Restore the interface or configure the route using the correct reachable next hop

symptom: R1 cannot learn the network behind R2 even though both routers are connected
topology: R1 -> R2 -> Server; OSPF is intended between R1 and R2
show_output: show ip ospf neighbor: no neighbors; show ip interface brief: R1 G0/1 10.0.0.1/30 up/up; R2 G0/0 10.0.0.2/30 up/up
expected_fault: OSPF adjacency is not forming between R1 and R2
expected_fix: Check OSPF configuration, area, router IDs, and interface participation on both routers

symptom: R1 and R2 form an OSPF neighbor relationship but R1 does not have a route to the server network
show_output: show ip ospf neighbor: R2 FULL; show ip route: no OSPF route to 192.168.30.0/24; R2 LAN: 192.168.30.0/24
expected_fault: The server network is not being advertised into OSPF by R2
expected_fix: Advertise 192.168.30.0/24 in the OSPF configuration on R2

symptom: Routers do not exchange routes using RIP
topology: R1 -> R2 -> R3; RIP is configured on all routers
show_output: show ip protocols: R1 uses RIP version 2; R2 uses RIP version 1
expected_fault: RIP version configuration is inconsistent between routers
expected_fix: Configure all routers to use the same RIP version

symptom: PC in VLAN 10 can reach the router but cannot reach the server in VLAN 30
topology: PC1 -> SW1 -> R1 -> Server; VLAN 10 and VLAN 30 are routed by R1
show_output: show access-lists: 10 deny ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 192.168.30.0 0.0.0.255; show ip interface g0/0: access group 10 in
expected_fault: ACL explicitly denies traffic from VLAN 10 to VLAN 30
expected_fix: Modify or remove the ACL rule that blocks VLAN 10 traffic to VLAN 30

symptom: Traffic that should be permitted is being blocked after an ACL was configured
show_output: show access-lists: 101 permit ip 192.168.10.0 0.0.0.255 any; show ip interface g0/0: access group 101 out
expected_fault: ACL is applied in the wrong direction for the intended traffic flow
expected_fix: Apply the ACL in the correct direction for the intended traffic

symptom: Guest users cannot access the internet even though the internet connection is working
show_output: show access-lists: 110 deny ip 192.168.50.0 0.0.0.255 any; show ip interface vlan 50: access group 110 in
expected_fault: ACL blocks all traffic from the guest VLAN
expected_fix: Change the ACL to permit the required guest traffic while keeping internal networks protected

symptom: Only one internal server can be reached while other permitted servers cannot
show_output: show access-lists: 120 permit ip host 192.168.10.10 host 192.168.30.10; no other permit statements
expected_fault: Traffic to other servers is blocked by the implicit deny at the end of the ACL
expected_fix: Add explicit permit rules for the required server destinations

symptom: Internal PCs can reach the router but cannot access the internet
topology: LAN -> R1 -> ISP Router -> Internet; internal network is 192.168.10.0/24
show_output: show ip nat translations: no translations; show running-config: no ip nat inside source configured
expected_fault: NAT overload is not configured for the internal network
expected_fix: Configure PAT/NAT overload for the internal network using the router's outside interface

symptom: Internal clients cannot access external networks after NAT was configured
show_output: show running-config interface g0/0: ip nat outside; show running-config interface g0/1: ip nat outside; LAN interface should be inside
expected_fault: The LAN interface is incorrectly configured as NAT outside instead of NAT inside
expected_fix: Configure the LAN-facing interface as ip nat inside

symptom: Some internal PCs can access the internet through NAT while others cannot
topology: LAN -> R1 -> ISP Router; LAN network is 192.168.10.0/24
show_output: access-list 1 permit 192.168.20.0 0.0.0.255; ip nat inside source list 1 interface g0/0 overload
expected_fault: NAT ACL permits the wrong internal network
expected_fix: Change the NAT ACL to permit the actual internal network 192.168.10.0/24

symptom: Wireless clients connect to the access point but cannot reach the internal network
topology: Wireless Client -> Access Point -> Switch -> R1; wireless clients should be placed in VLAN 50
show_output: show vlan brief: VLAN 50 active; show interfaces trunk: VLAN 50 not allowed on trunk between switch and access point
expected_fault: Wireless client VLAN is not being carried across the trunk
expected_fix: Allow VLAN 50 on the trunk connecting the switch and wireless access point

symptom: Wireless clients can connect to the SSID but cannot obtain an IP address
topology: Wireless Client -> Access Point -> Switch -> R1; DHCP server provides addresses for VLAN 50
show_output: show ip interface vlan 50: 192.168.50.1/24 up/up; show running-config interface vlan 50: no ip helper-address; DHCP server: 192.168.10.10
expected_fault: DHCP relay is missing for the wireless client VLAN
expected_fix: Configure ip helper-address 192.168.10.10 on the VLAN 50 interface
